stemMd: In which programme was the employment rate (employed respondents as a share of all respondents in that programme) closest to the employment rate of all 400 respondents?
instructionsMd: Use only the figures shown. Work by hand.
explanationMd:
The overall rate is $\frac{286}{400} = 71.5$ per cent. The programme rates are

$$\text{Economics } \tfrac{120}{160} = 75\% \quad \text{Engineering } \tfrac{96}{120} = 80\% \quad \text{Humanities } \tfrac{44}{80} = 55\% \quad \text{Law } \tfrac{26}{40} = 65\%$$

The distances from 71.5 are 3.5, 8.5, 16.5 and 6.5 points. Economics is closest.

**Why this makes sense.** The overall rate is a weighted average of the programme rates, weighted by respondents. Economics is the largest programme, 160 of 400, so it pulls the overall figure towards its own rate.

distractorRationale.d: Engineering's rate is $\frac{96}{120} = 80$ per cent, 8.5 points above the overall 71.5 per cent. It has the highest rate, not the closest.
distractorRationale.a: Humanities, at $\frac{44}{80} = 55$ per cent, is the furthest from the overall rate, 16.5 points below it.
distractorRationale.b: Law's rate is $\frac{26}{40} = 65$ per cent, 6.5 points below the overall rate: closer than Engineering or Humanities, but not as close as Economics at 3.5 points.

accessibilityText: A question about the table of 400 surveyed graduates. It asks in which programme the employment rate was closest to the overall employment rate of all 400 respondents. The options are the four programmes: Economics, Engineering, Humanities, Law.

provenance.notes: Original item. Rates are 75, 80, 55 and 65 per cent against an overall 71.5 per cent, so the nearest is unambiguous.
